readings.title: Tragedy in Moab
readings.text: [Ruth 1:1] And it came to be in the days when the judges ruled, that there was a famine in the land. And a man from Bĕyth Leḥem, Yehuḏah, went to sojourn in the fields of Mo’aḇ, he and his wife and his two sons. [2] And the name of the man was Elimelek, and the name of his wife Naʽomi, and the names of his two sons were Maḥlon and Kilyon – Ephrathites of Bĕyth Leḥem, Yehuḏah. And they went to the fields of Mo’aḇ and came to be there. [3] And Elimelek, husband of Naʽomi, died, and she was left with her two sons. [4] And they took wives of the women of Mo’aḇ: the name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other Ruth. And they dwelt there about ten years. [5] And both Maḥlon and Kilyon also died. So the woman was left of her two children and of her husband.

readings.title: The Loyalty of Ruth
readings.text: [Ruth 1:6] And she rose up, she and her daughters-in-law, and returned from the fields of Mo’aḇ, for she had heard in the fields of Mo’aḇ that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had visited <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> people by giving them bread. [7] Therefore she went out from the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her. And they went on the way to return to the land of Yehuḏah. [8] And Naʽomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go, return each to her mother’s house. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> show kindness to you, as you have done with the dead and with me. [9] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> grant that you find rest, each in the house of her husband.” Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their voice and wept. [10] And they said to her, “No, we shall return with you to your people.” [11] And Naʽomi said, “Turn back, my daughters, why go with me? Are there still sons in my womb, that they should become your husbands? [12] “Turn back, my daughters, go, for I am too old to have a husband. If I should say I have hope, if I should have a husband tonight and should also bear sons, [13] would you wait for them till they were grown? Would you shut yourselves up for them and not have a husband? No, my daughters, for it is much more bitter for me than for you that the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has gone out against me!” [14] And they lifted up their voice and wept again. And Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her. [15] And she said, “Look, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her mighty ones. Return after your sister-in-law.” [16] But Ruth said, “Do not urge me to leave you, or to go back from following after you. For wherever you go, I go; and wherever you lodge, I lodge; your people is my people, and your <dn>Elohim</dn> is my <dn>Elohim</dn>. [17] “Where you die, I die, and there I shall be buried. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> do so to me, and more also, if anything but death parts you and me.” [18] And when she saw that she was steadfastly minded to go with her, she ceased speaking to her.

readings.title: Return to Bethlehem
readings.text: [Ruth 1:19] And both of them went until they came to Bĕyth Leḥem. And it came to be, when they had come to Bĕyth Leḥem, that all the city was moved because of them, and they said, “Is this Naʽomi?” [20] And she said to them, “Do not call me Naʽomi, call me Mara, for <dn>Shaddai</dn> has dealt very bitterly with me. [21] “I went out full, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has brought me back empty. Why do you call me Naʽomi, since <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has witnessed against me, and <dn>Shaddai</dn> has done evil to me?” [22] And Naʽomi returned, and Ruth the Mo’aḇitess her daughter-in-law with her, who returned from the fields of Mo’aḇ. And they came to Bĕyth Leḥem at the beginning of barley harvest.

readings.title: Gleaning in the Fields
readings.text: [Ruth 2:1] And Naʽomi had a relative of her husband’s, a man of great wealth, of the family of Elimelek. His name was Boʽaz. [2] And Ruth the Mo’aḇitess said to Naʽomi, “Please let me go to the field, and glean heads of grain after him in whose eyes I find favor.” And she said to her, “Go, my daughter.” [3] And she went and came and gleaned in the field after the reapers. And she happened to come to the part of the field belonging to Boʽaz, who was of the family of Elimelek. [4] And see, Boʽaz came from Bĕyth Leḥem, and said to the reapers, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be with you!” And they answered him, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> bless you!” [5] And Boʽaz said to his servant who was set over the reapers, “Whose young woman is this?” [6] And the servant who was set over the reapers answered and said, “It is the young Mo’aḇite woman who came back with Naʽomi from the fields of Mo’aḇ, [7] and she said, ‘Please let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves.’ And she came and has remained from the morning until now – she sat a little in the house.” [8] And Boʽaz said to Ruth, “Have you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, nor go from here, but stay close by my young women. [9] “Let your eyes be on the field which they reap, and you shall go after them. Have I not commanded the young men not to touch you? And when you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink from what the young men have drawn.” [10] And she fell on her face, bowed down to the ground, and said to him, “Why have I found favor in your eyes, that you should take notice of me, seeing I am a foreigner?” [11] And Boʽaz answered and said to her, “I have been fully told of <dn>את</dn> all that you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband, and how you have left your father and your mother and the land of your birth, and have come to a people whom you did not know before. [12] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> repay your work, and your reward be perfect from <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, under whose wings you have come to seek refuge.” [13] And she said, “Let me find favor in your eyes, my master, because you have comforted me, and have spoken to the heart of your female servant, though I am not like one of your female servants.”

readings.title: Favor Found
readings.text: [Ruth 2:14] And Boʽaz said to her at mealtime, “Come here, and eat of the bread, and dip your piece of bread in the vinegar.” And she sat beside the reapers, and he passed parched grain to her. And she ate and was satisfied, and had some left over. [15] And she rose up to glean. And Boʽaz commanded his young men, saying, “Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not reproach her. [16] “And also draw out for her from the bundles, and leave it for her to glean, and do not reprove her.” [17] And she gleaned in the field until evening, and beat out <dn>את</dn> what she had gleaned, and it was about an ĕphah of barley. [18] And she took it up and went into the city, and her mother-in-law saw <dn>את</dn> what she had gleaned. And she brought out and gave to her <dn>את</dn> what she had kept back after she had been satisfied. [19] And her mother-in-law said to her, “Where have you gleaned today? And where did you work? Blessed be the one who took notice of you.” And she told her mother-in-law <dn>את</dn> with whom she had worked, and said, “The man’s name with whom I worked today is Boʽaz.” [20] And Naʽomi said to her daughter-in-law, “Blessed be he of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who has not forsaken <dn>His</dn> kindness to the living and the dead!” And Naʽomi said to her, “The man is a relative of ours, one of our redeemers.” [21] And Ruth the Mo’aḇitess said, “He also said to me, ‘Stay close by my young men until they have finished all my harvest.’ ” [22] And Naʽomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, and that they do not meet you in any other field.” [23] And she stayed close by the young women of Boʽaz, to glean until the end of barley harvest and wheat harvest, and dwelt with her mother-in-law.

readings.title: The Threshing Floor
readings.text: [Ruth 3:1] And Naʽomi her mother-in-law said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek rest for you, so that it might be well with you? [2] “And now, is not Boʽaz, with whose young women you have been, our relative? See, he is winnowing <dn>את</dn> barley tonight at the threshing-floor. [3] “And you shall bathe and anoint yourself, and put your outer garments on and go down to the threshing-floor. Do not make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking. [4] “And it shall be, when he lies down, that you shall notice <dn>את</dn> the place where he lies. And you shall go in, and uncover <dn>את</dn> his feet, and lie down. And let him tell you <dn>את</dn> what you should do.” [5] And she said to her, “All that you say to me I do.” [6] And she went down to the threshing-floor and did according to all that her mother-in-law commanded her. [7] And Boʽaz ate and drank, and his heart was glad, and he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. And she came softly, and uncovered his feet, and lay down. [8] And it came to be at midnight that the man was startled, and turned himself, and see, a woman was lying at his feet. [9] And he said, “Who are you?” And she answered, “I am Ruth, your female servant. Now you shall spread your covering over your female servant, for you are a redeemer.” [10] And he said, “Blessed are you of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, my daughter! For you have shown more kindness at the end than at the beginning, in not going after young men, whether poor or rich. [11] “And now, my daughter, do not fear. I do for you <dn>את</dn> all that you say, for all the gate of my people know that you are a capable woman. [12] “And now, it is true that I am a redeemer, but there is a redeemer nearer than I. [13] “Stay this night, and in the morning it shall be: if he redeems you, good – let him redeem. But if he does not wish to redeem you, then I shall redeem you, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives. Lie down until morning.” [14] And she lay at his feet until morning, and she rose up before one could recognize another. Then he said, “Do not let it be known that the woman came to the threshing-floor.” [15] And he said, “Bring the shawl that is on you and hold it.” And when she held it, he measured six measures of barley, and laid it on her. Then he went into the city. [16] And she came to her mother-in-law, and she said, “Who are you, my daughter?” And she told her <dn>את</dn> all that the man had done for her. [17] And she said, “These six measures of barley he gave me, for he said to me, ‘Do not go empty to your mother-in-law.’ ” [18] Then she said, “Sit still, my daughter, until you know how the matter falls, for the man is not going to rest until he has completed the matter this day.”

readings.title: The Kinsman Redeemer
readings.text: [Ruth 4:1] And Boʽaz went up to the gate and sat down there. And see, the redeemer of whom Boʽaz had spoken came by. And he said, “O such and such, turn aside, sit down here.” And he turned aside and sat down. [2] And he took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, “Sit down here.” And they sat down. [3] And he said to the redeemer, “Naʽomi, who has come back from the fields of Mo’aḇ, sold <dn>את</dn> the piece of land which belonged to our brother Elimelek. [4] “And I thought that I should disclose it to you, saying, ‘Buy it in the presence of the inhabitants and the elders of my people. If you redeem, redeem. But if you do not redeem, tell me, so that I know. For there is no one but you to redeem it, and I am after you.’ ” And he said, “I redeem.” [5] And Boʽaz said, “On the day you buy the field from the hand of Naʽomi, you shall also buy it from Ruth the Mo’aḇitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance.” [6] And the redeemer said, “I am not able to redeem it for myself, lest I ruin my own inheritance. You redeem <dn>את</dn> my right of redemption for yourself, for I am not able to redeem.” [7] Now this was the custom in former times in Yisra’ĕl concerning redeeming and exchanging, to confirm every word: one man took off his sandal and gave it to the other, and this was a witness in Yisra’ĕl. [8] So the redeemer said to Boʽaz, “Buy it for yourself,” and he took off his sandal. [9] And Boʽaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses this day that I have bought <dn>את</dn> all that was Elimelek’s, and <dn>את</dn> all that was Kilyon’s and Maḥlon’s, from the hand of Naʽomi. [10] “And also <dn>את</dn> Ruth the Mo’aḇitess, the wife of Maḥlon, I have acquired as my wife, to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance, so that the name of the dead is not cut off from among his brothers and from the gate of his place. You are witnesses this day.” [11] And all the people who were at the gate, and the elders, said, “Witnesses! <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> make <dn>את</dn> the woman who is coming to your house like Raḥĕl and like Lĕ’ah, the two who built <dn>את</dn> the house of Yisra’ĕl. And present yourself worthily in Ephrathah and proclaim the name in Bĕyth Leḥem. [12] “And let your house be like the house of Perets, whom Tamar bore to Yehuḏah, of the seed which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gives you from this young woman.”
